lessons: hayscad.com/data-downloads/ 403s any fetch with no User-Agent header (matches lib/cad-ingest/src/sources.ts's documented WAF note) but returns 200 to a plain curl carrying a standard browser User-Agent -- no cookies, no JS challenge, no auth needed. Any future Hays acquisition work that needs to enumerate available drops programmatically should set a UA header rather than treating the page as unreachable; this is not the OAuth/credential-rotation trap the CANON-PREAMBLE warns about (COTALITY IS EXTINGUISHED), it is a bare bot-UA block.

Hays CAD publishes at least two structurally DIFFERENT export schemas for the same roll: the informal 'PropertyDataExport' CSV convention (PropertyID, MarketValue, Situs columns -- what the current orion parser reads) used for preliminary/as-of snapshots, and their own 'Orion Certified Export' naming (PropertyQuickRefID, no MarketValue/Situs columns, values likely live in a companion file within that same zip) used for the certified release. The current classifyOrionHeader (lib/cad-ingest/src/orion/parser.ts:69-75) cannot read the second shape at all -- it would classify it 'unknown' and the CLI would hard-fail (rowsParsed===0), which is a safe failure, not a silent one, but it means the certified export is NOT currently an ingestable source for Hays even though it is Hays CAD's own most-official release.

cad_property's source_file/source_vintage fields reflect LAST WRITER, not full provenance -- a later upsert (e.g. the P-78 StratMap fallback) overwrites those fields for any row it touches, even a row that originally came from a different source and was merely updated. Counting rows by source_file after multiple layered applies to the same tax_year will undercount the original source's true contribution. Any future acquisition-record archaeology on a county with more than one applied layer at the same tax_year should expect this and cross-check against a filed announce/apply-log artifact (P-78's, in this case) rather than trusting source_file alone as a partition.

No ingest-run-log mechanism exists anywhere in this program (no cad_ingest_runs table, no per-run JSON artifact). This lane worked around it by recounting the source directly, which the dispatch itself anticipated and required ('do not infer it from the shape of cad_property'). Proposing, not building (DEV_PROCESS 5.4 -- propose, do not unilaterally remediate; out of this dispatch's scope): a lightweight per-run log (source URL/file, row counts reported, success/fail, timestamp) would have let this question be answered by reading a table instead of re-downloading and re-parsing 40MB+ zip files three times.
deadEnds: WebFetch on https://hayscad.com/data-downloads/ returns a bare 403 with no body -- do not retry it plain; it needs a browser User-Agent via curl/Bash instead.
